School of Inquisimancy

Wizard Subclass

Inquisimancy is a secret school of magic known by only a few select families. Those who know the magic are often close advisors to the king, who interrogate spies or captured soldiers for information about the kingdom’s enemies. A more sinister form of magic is often used in torture, breaking the minds of even the most resilient of targets. There are whispers amongst the common folk about such practices, though most dismiss them as just folk tales meant to dissuade them from rebelling or breaking the law. To Inquisimancers, the mind is a playground to be manipulated and pulled until its secrets pour out. They are often curious people, seeking out mystery and the unknown in an endless pursuit of knowledge.

Wizard Level Features
2nd Inquisimancy Savant, Read Emotion
6th Ace Detective
10th Mind Bender
14th Rupture Sanity

Inquisimancy Spells Table

The following spells are added to the wizard spell list for you, though you still must add them to your spellbook before being able to cast them.

Wizard Level Spells
1st Coax Truth, Assault Mind
3rd Psychic Whip
5th Scramble
7th Freeze

Ace Detective

Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, when you fail an Insight, Perception, or Investigation check, you may expend a spell slot to add a d6 to the roll. You add an additional d6 for every 2 slot levels above 1st.

Read Emotion

Starting at the 2nd level, when you choose this school, you can use magic to dial in what your target is feeling and thinking at the current moment. As a bonus action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 ft to begin reading. The creature must have an Intelligence score greater than 4. For the next minute, it is unable to surprise you and you gain advantage on Insight. Once the effect ends, you cannot use this feature again until the end of a long rest.

Maim Psyche

Beginning at the 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals psychic damage, you may reroll a number of damage dice up to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). You must use the new roll(s). When you deal psychic damage to a creature affected by Read Emotion, you deal an additional d6 of psychic damage. You gain an extra use of the Read Emotion feat.

Mind Bender

Beginning at the 10th level, your expertise in the minds of others allows you to be more accurate in your spell casting. A creature that is affected by your Read Emotions has disadvantage on Saving Throws against your spells and you have Advantage on Spell Attack rolls against them. You gain an extra use of the Read Emotion feat.

Rupture Sanity

Beginning at the 14th level, you are a master of manipulating the minds of others, allowing you to temporarily destroy their mental stability, forcing them to become mindless, insane creatures. As an action, choose a creature you can see within 15 ft. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC. Upon failure, the creature’s mind is broken. At the start of their turn, they must roll a d10 to determine their action for the round. They reroll the saving throw at the end of their turn. Once the effect ends or if the creature succeeds the check, you cannot use this feature again until the end of a long rest.

Insanity Table

d10 Insanity Effect
1 As their mind tries to repair itself, it causes a splitting headache, dealing 4d6 Psychic damage. Their turn ends.
2 The creature’s mind falls into further disrepair and they are Stunned until the start of their next turn. Their turn ends.
3 The creature envisions monsters crawling all over their skin, forcing them to use their action to target themselves with the strongest attack they have. Their turn ends.
4 The creature is put into a rage-like state as they attack the creature that is closest to them. Their turn ends.
5 The creature is frightened of the Inquisimancy Wizard, using their action to Dash and run away from the wizard. Their turn ends.
6 The creature feels famished, they eat whatever object is held in their hands. If they are holding nothing, they grab the nearest creature and attempt to eat them. Their turn ends. The creature wanders in a random direction. Their turn ends.
7 The creature spins until they fall prone because of dizziness. Their turn ends.
8 The creature babbles random nonsense. Their turn ends.
9 The creature wanders in a random direction. Their Turn Ends
10 The creature momentarily becomes sane, using their actions and movement however they like. However, their sanity slips away when they end their turn.

Playtested By:

  • ▶ @sydneyry8n - Anthelme Sylvain (Level 9)
    My character Anthelme used the School of Inquisimancy as both a prominent feature in his backstory and in his primary method of magical contribution to the party. For the former, this magic focus led to a complicated relationship between Anthelme and his own morality—his main character development during the campaign was softening from the self-loathing, closed-off person he was, realizing that he was not a monster and that he did deserve close and honest relationships. For the latter, he used the inquisimancy spells in combat to confuse/damage enemies and during interrogations (the canon use of it). I also found them to be a good opportunity for cool fight scenes and descriptive attacks, as a lot of the spells include a sensory experience for the enemy.
